updates.name: Peter J. Edmunds
updates.bio: California State University Northridge biologist whose lab studies the physiological ecology of tropical reef corals through combined laboratory and field experiments. The lab follows long-term reef dynamics alongside individual coral biology, aiming to project how coral populations will respond to global climate change. NSF supports its LTER work in Moorea and LTREB work in St. John, USVI.
updates.research_interests: physiological ecology of tropical reef corals; long-term coral reef dynamics; cellular and subcellular processes in corals; projecting coral population change under climate change

updates.name: Robert C. Carpenter
updates.bio: California State University Northridge ecologist studying marine benthic communities: how light and water flow shape algal physiology, and how herbivore-algae interactions scale up to communities, comparing coral reefs with kelp forests. One of four PIs of the Moorea Coral Reef LTER, measuring long-term change in reef structure and function and hydrodynamic controls on reef metabolism.
updates.research_interests: marine benthic community ecology; light and water flow effects on algal physiology; herbivore-algae interactions; coral reef metabolism and hydrodynamics; coral reef versus kelp forest communities
updates.evidence: As one of 4 PIs on this project, I am involved in quantifying long-term changes in coral reef community structure and function.
updates.notes: Gump Station people page (Moorea) is a profile of this person at California State University Northridge and names the NSF LTER coral reef site in Moorea. Existing ORCID 0000-0003-4232-1868 checked at pub.orcid.org: name Robert Carpenter, employment California State University Northridge, Professor, 1988-present (consistent); title taken from that employment. No Google Scholar link found. No page states active/emeritus, so status left null.

updates.name: Adam Davis
updates.bio: Heads the Department of Crop Sciences at the University of Illinois, where he is a professor recognized internationally for agroecology centred on ecological approaches to weed control. He uses field experiments and models to tackle applied weed problems in crop production, including herbicide resistance evolution and spread, multi-tactic integrated weed management, weed seedbank ecology and diversified cropping systems.
updates.research_interests: diversified cropping systems and agroecosystem sustainability; spatial ecology of agricultural risk and plant invasions; herbicide resistance evolution; integrated weed management; weed seedbank ecology
updates.current_title: Professor and Department Head, Department of Crop Sciences

updates.name: Frederick E. Below
updates.bio: Crop physiology professor in Crop Sciences at the University of Illinois. His research asks what limits the productivity of corn and soybean. He teaches crop courses from introductory to graduate level and devised the corn 'Seven Wonders' and soybean 'Six Secrets' frameworks to show farmers and agricultural professionals how each management decision affects yield.
updates.research_interests: grain quality for processing; nitrogen use efficiency and nutrient uptake and partitioning; corn and soybean production management; fertilizer placement and timing; crop rotation and tillage effects

updates.name: Jonathan Coppess
updates.bio: Associate Professor of law and policy in Agricultural and Consumer Economics at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and director of its Gardner Agriculture Policy Program. Research centres on agricultural law and policy, covering farm support, risk management, natural resource conservation and biofuels. Teaches the department's agricultural law course.
updates.research_interests: agricultural law and policy; farm support programs and risk management; conservation of natural resources; biofuels
